subject: Interim update: Dedicated pool saturation affecting Spectra Analytics
messages:
From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
To: Saira Patel <saira@spectra.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 30 Jun 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Interim update: Dedicated pool saturation affecting Spectra Analytics

Hi Saira —

Quick update from our side on the dedicated GPU pool event that started overnight and impacted some of Spectra's inference traffic:

What we saw
- Between 02:10–03:45 UTC the reserved nodes assigned to your pool experienced sustained queueing and increased warmup latency tied to a sudden spike in concurrent batch starts.
- This manifested as generation latency >3x your normal 99th percentile and intermittent rate-limit throttles from our scheduling layer.

Immediate actions taken
- Ops scaled a short-term buffer by bringing two warm standby nodes into your reserved pool (applied at 02:58 UTC).
- We temporarily enabled our fallback routing for low-priority traffic to a quantized model variant (this preserved completion for interactive flows while avoiding the warmup overhead).
- Autoscaler patch deployed at 03:22 UTC to correct an incorrect cool-down heuristic that prevented timely node activation.

Customer-facing impact
- You may have seen elevated latencies for about ~95 minutes and a small percentage of throttled requests. We believe the majority of user-facing requests completed under the fallback path.

Next steps and asks
- We will provide a full evidence packet (allocation traces, scheduler logs, and warmup timelines) within 24 hours. I attached a brief allocation snapshot for immediate context.
- Can you confirm if we have permission to: 1) temporarily route a small percentage of your traffic (<=10%) to a slightly lower-precision model for 4 hours if we need to avoid degraded UX during any future mitigations, and 2) ingest your request pattern file for the affected window (we only use it for post-incident analysis)?

Proposed follow-up
- 14:00 PT call today to walk the packet and commercial remediation (credits). If that time doesn't work, tell me a slot.

Apologies for the disruption — we know this impacts your SLAs and we are prioritizing closure and compensation.

Attachments: allocation-snapshot-20280630.csv (summary), ops-fallback-rfc.md

Thanks,
Ben
Account Exec, Redwood Inference

From: Saira Patel <saira@spectra.ai>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 30 Jun 2028 10:05:12 -0700
Subject: Re: Interim update: Dedicated pool saturation affecting Spectra Analytics

Ben —

Thanks for the quick note and for moving additional capacity. A couple of quick questions before the 14:00 PT call:

1) Can you quantify the percent of our requests that were routed to the quantized fallback? We need that to validate user-impact.
2) Will the autoscaler patch require any restart or downtime to our reserved pool?
3) We will need transaction-level logs for the window 02:00–04:30 UTC to reconcile with our observability (request IDs suffice).

We're ok with routing a small percentage to a lower-precision model for an emergency window provided you share the expected UX delta and it only applies during active mitigation. You can route up to 10% as you suggested; please also note any rate limit anomalies so we can map them on our side.

I attached our initial request-ID list in case that speeds the match.

—Saira
Head of Platform, Spectra Analytics
attachments: spectra_req_ids_0628.csv

Forwarding Saira's reply. Commercial quick notes:
- They asked for percent-routed and transaction-level logs (we can provide both).
- Suggest offering a one-week service credit equal to 30% of June committed usage as a gesture; we've used similar bands for this class of disruption. I can draft the credit note and a short FAQ for their Finance contact.
- Confirm we will not proactively change their model configuration except under explicit permission (they gave conditional permission for <=10% routing).

Ops ask: can we prepare the evidence packet and a short ops-runbook (two-page) describing the autoscaler fix + the fallback activation conditions. Karthik — can you confirm L2/engineering availability for the 14:00 PT call?

Marissa
Director, Customer Success

Date: Tue, 30 Jun 2028 14:03:05 -0700
Subject: Re: Interim update: Dedicated pool saturation affecting Spectra Analytics

Saira / team —

Thanks for the swift reply and for granting conditional routing permission. Short answers before our call:

1) Percent routed: preliminary scheduler traces show ~8.7% of completed requests for the 02:10–03:45 UTC window took the fallback path. We'll include the per-minute breakdown in the evidence packet.
2) Autoscaler patch: the hotfix is non-disruptive; it's a tuning change to the cool-down window and was applied without restarts. We validated node activation behaviour in the canary pool prior to rollout.
3) Transaction logs: we are preparing a zipped evidence packet containing per-request traces, request IDs (matched to your file), node allocation timelines, and the autoscaler event log. Expect delivery to the Drive link below within ~3 hours.

Commercials and remediation
- We will offer a one-week credit note equivalent to 30% of your June committed reserved spend (see attached credit draft). Marissa will follow up on the precise language and sign-off process.

Follow-up call
- Confirmed: 14:00 PT today. Agenda: walkthrough of evidence packet, RCA draft (timeline + root cause), and commercial remediation. Joining: Karthik (L2), Jordan (SRE), Marissa (CS).

Attachments delivered after call: spectra_evidence_packet_20280630.zip (contains allocation traces and per-request mapping), ops-fallback-rfc.md (fallback activation conditions), allocation-snapshot-20280630.csv

Thanks again for your patience. We will close the RCA and publish the postmortem with P0 headings within 5 business days; a full internal RCA with follow-through actions will be published within 14 days.

Ben
Account Exec, Redwood Inference
